name: Direct lateral hip approach (Hardinge/transgluteal)
corridor: Transgluteal split through the anterior gluteus medius and minimus, continued distally through vastus lateralis

positioning.text: Position the patient supine or lateral with the greater trochanter accessible and the leg free for manipulation.

setup.text: Prep the operative limb freely so rotation, adduction, and extension can be used during femoral exposure.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the greater trochanter, femoral shaft, and the longitudinal axis of the proximal femur.

incision.text: Center a longitudinal incision over the greater trochanter and extend distally along the lateral femoral shaft as required.

superficial_interval.text: Incise fascia lata in line with the skin incision and expose the gluteus medius insertion and proximal vastus lateralis.

deep_interval.text: Split the anterior portion of gluteus medius in line with its fibers, continue through gluteus minimus, and carry the sleeve distally into vastus lateralis.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, anterior gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, and hip capsule; the distal exposure continues through vastus lateralis.

structures_encountered.text: The anterior abductor sleeve is elevated from the greater trochanter while preserving tissue for secure repair.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve is endangered by excessive proximal splitting of gluteus medius.
The abductor mechanism is at risk if the anterior sleeve is damaged or inadequately repaired.

danger_zones.text: Limit the proximal gluteus medius split to the safe distance described for the exposure and do not extend blindly toward the superior gluteal neurovascular bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Place acetabular and femoral retractors directly on bone and avoid deep posterior placement that could threaten the sciatic nerve.

exposure.text: Provides broad access to the lateral proximal femur, femoral neck, and hip joint for arthroplasty and selected proximal-femoral procedures.

limitations.text: The approach violates part of the abductor mechanism and can produce postoperative limp or weakness if the split or repair is inadequate.

extensions.text: Extend distally along the lateral femur through vastus lateralis when additional shaft or implant access is needed.

indications.text: Commonly used for hip hemiarthroplasty and total hip arthroplasty and adaptable to procedures requiring lateral proximal-femoral exposure.

relative_contraindications.text: Consider an alternative when pre-existing abductor deficiency makes further transgluteal injury unacceptable or when the required exposure lies outside this corridor.

implant_implications.text: Preserve enough anterior abductor–vastus sleeve for repair and ensure the exposure permits controlled femoral preparation without levering on the greater trochanter.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: When imaging is required, confirm that positioning and draping allow unobstructed AP and lateral views before incision.

closure.text: Repair capsule as indicated and securely reattach the anterior gluteus medius–minimus–vastus sleeve before closing fascia lata, subcutaneous tissue, and skin.

complications.text: Approach-specific complications include superior gluteal nerve injury, abductor insufficiency, Trendelenburg gait, heterotopic ossification, and general arthroplasty complications.

bailouts.text: If femoral access is inadequate, extend the lateral exposure in a controlled fashion rather than enlarging the proximal abductor split or applying forceful retraction.

questions.question: Which nerve limits proximal extension of the direct lateral approach?
What functional complication follows failed abductor repair?
questions.answer: Abductor weakness with a Trendelenburg limp or gait.
